title: Console Onramp: Surgical MVP Slice for Dashboards, Tracing, and Cost Details
creator: Leah Kim
description: This ticket defines a surgical reduction of Console features for initial GA onramp: keep a minimal but useful dashboard surface, add a lightweight trace sampler integration, and provide a compact cost-breakdown card. The goal is to deliver usable observability for early customers while deferring heavyweight features that increase build time and egress costs.
background: Multiple stakeholder discussions in Q1 identified that full-featured dashboards, deep trace explorers, and per-token cost visualizations push the Console beyond a 6-week onramp. We need a pragmatic MVP that demonstrates value to engineering customers (route-level latency, simple traces, and cost summaries) while leaving advanced rollouts, deep trace tabbing, and per-request token flamegraphs for later phases.
scope_in: One dashboard landing page with 4 compact cards: Route latency summary, Error rate trend, Request volume, Cost snapshot (aggregated by route)
Simple trace link from a sample request: open lightweight trace viewer that shows span tree up to 1 second of depth and highlights top 5 spans by duration
Cost snapshot card: daily and 7d token-equivalent cost approximation by route with hover-to-see top-3 routes
Rollout gating: feature flag per-organization to enable the compact dashboard
Acceptance tests and e2e smoke tests for the compact dashboard and trace sampler
scope_out: Full trace explorer with span-level filtering, query language, and arbitrary time ranges
Drilldown dashboards with arbitrary pivoting and custom cards
High-cardinality metrics indexing and long retention for MVP (deferred to telemetry infra project)
Automated A/B cost vs quality prompt analytics
decisions: Ship a single landing dashboard instead of multiple detailed dashboards to reduce design and infra work
Implement a trace sampler that surfaces a single representative trace per route per hour instead of full retention
Expose cost as aggregated snapshot (USD approximation) using existing billing data; defer precise per-token cost to Optimize feature
Feature gated by organization with opt-in SDK guidance to minimize unexpected load
tradeoffs: Simplicity vs depth: the compact surface reduces discoverability of edge cases but accelerates shipping and decreases storage/ejection costs
Accuracy vs speed: cost estimates will be approximate (USD heuristics) to avoid an expensive per-token join at MVP
Developer ergonomics vs implementation time: lightweight trace viewer is less powerful but requires minimal changes to trace storage schema
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Landing dashboard renders for orgs with feature flag enabled within 1.5s cold load and <600ms subsequent navigations
AC-2: All 4 compact cards populate with data for last 24 hours and show non-empty states when telemetry available
AC-3: Clicking a route on the Route latency card opens a lightweight trace viewer showing a tree with span durations and highlights top-5 spans; viewer loads <800ms for sampled traces
AC-4: Cost snapshot matches billing pipeline daily totals within +/-10% for aggregated route groups in test orgs
AC-5: E2E smoke tests run in CI and pass against staging with synthetic events; include a synthetic long-tail latency trace
AC-6: Feature is behind org-level flag and onboarding UX includes a short tooltip explaining limits of MVP data
AC-7: Rollout checklist completed: design signoff, security review (not required for MVP), infra readiness, runbook for degraded telemetry
success_metrics: M1: 75% of early access orgs that opt in view dashboard daily in first 14 days
M2: Median dashboard load time <1.2s in production for 95th percentile of requests
M3: Support tickets related to missing telemetry for the MVP surface < 5 for first 30 days
M4: Observed cost of telemetry ingestion for MVP surface increases infra cost by <12% over baseline
rollout_plan: Week 0: Merge MVP PR and run canary in one internal org
Week 1: Invite 5 beta customers to opt in (manual enable via console or API)
Week 2: Monitor success metrics and APM traces for regressions; expand to 20 orgs if stable
Week 3: Open public onramp with doc links and SDK guidance; enable default-off flag for new orgs
Rollback criteria: any sustained 5xx increase >2x baseline or dashboard load regressions >300ms for more than 15 minutes
risks: Under-indexed telemetry could result in empty cards for low-traffic orgs (mitigation: show helpful empty states and sampling guidance)
Cost heuristics may underreport for organizations with reserve pricing or Dedicated contracts (mitigation: label as estimated and add link to Billing)
Trace sampler could miss causal traces for very spiky workloads (mitigation: allow ad-hoc manual sampling via SDK for early partners)
Visibility: customers may expect parity with full tracing products — messaging must set expectations
dependencies: ENG-73421: telemetry ingestion sampling rules (sampling hook for Console)
ENG-76210: billing pipeline daily aggregation endpoint
DES-1192: compact-card visual components and accessible colors
ENG-78001: feature flagging infra for org-level toggles
